ranked.headline: Fast, accurate qLDPC decoders and optimized syndrome-extraction circuits converge
ranked.summary: Several new qLDPC decoders report latency and accuracy gains over BP+OSD, Relay-BP and BP-LSD, alongside new circuit-scheduling and code-design tools.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is decoding quantum LDPC codes accurately within real-time budgets. SCOPE, a physics-informed parallel decoder, reports a logical error rate of 4.82e-10 on the [[144,12,12]] bivariate bicycle code with 173.8 ns latency. TEMPO-BP adapts per-variable memory strength through local feedback and lowers failure rates relative to BP+OSD and Relay-BP. TCBP-JOBS learns calibrated fault probabilities on GPUs and matches Tesseract accuracy. A hybrid sliding-window decoder for trapped-ion noise uses soft-output confidence to switch windows, improving on BP-LSD. For surface codes, Beyond Blossom reports a 4.23x geometric-mean speedup for CPU MWPM via local predecoding. A second strand targets syndrome-extraction circuits: Proxima schedules them with a DEM-based proximity metric, and structure-guided CP-SAT synthesis lowers logical error rates for CSS qLDPC codes. Code design adds Armillary codes with rates above 1/2 for fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware and rate-optimal distance-3 and distance-4 color codes. Two Ising-machine papers sit outside this thread.

ranked.headline: Simulations quantify modelling biases in lensing, clustering and halo-bias inference
ranked.summary: Preprints use TNG, HR4, HESTIA and baryonified N-body runs to quantify biases in H0, w0wa, fNL and assembly-bias inference for Euclid- and DESI-era analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulations to calibrate systematics and secondary dependencies between observables and cosmological parameters. Among nuisance effects, on-the-fly Gaussian Process reconstruction of n(z) in Euclid-like 3×2pt analyses shows that redshift-distribution errors bias w0wa. IllustrisTNG ellipticals indicate that multipole mass terms bias time-delay H0 by 1–6%. Light-cone and relativistic effects bias local fNL by about 2σ in a Euclid-like survey and by more than 10σ in a MegaMapper-like survey. Baryonification V generates tSZ Compton-y maps from dark-matter-only light cones. For secondary bias, TNG300 attributes halo secondary bias largely to the unbound matter fraction in the circum-halo medium. Luminosity-weighted marked correlations are proposed as an assembly-bias null test on DESI-BGS mocks. In observation–simulation comparisons, SDSS genus topology agrees with modern HR4 galaxy models, and Local Group satellite-pair statistics are compared with HESTIA. More peripheral work includes a GR test using DESI Legacy cluster clustering and a Gini-index analysis of BCG dominance that finds no evolution.

ranked.headline: Co-designed FPGA and GPU control stacks target microsecond real-time QEC decoding
ranked.summary: Several preprints report sub-microsecond decoding and QEC-loop closure on FPGAs, making classical control latency a concrete design target for fault tolerance.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is co-design of the classical hardware that must keep pace with fault-tolerant quantum processors. On decoding, Rapids pairs a streaming neural decoder with FPGAs to decode surface-code syndromes in under a microsecond, reporting lower logical error rates than existing decoders. Pêlagos orchestrates relay belief-propagation decoding across multiple GPUs under real-time constraints. A survey organizes hierarchical decoding by decoder- and code-level hierarchy, platforms and latency trade-offs. CHEQ evaluates decoders concurrently on an FPGA via geometric-skip circuit-level noise sampling, matching Stim firing rates within 0.16%. QuFrame's control microarchitecture closes the QEC loop within 1 μs through real-time Pauli frame tracking. A second strand addresses platform-specific compilation and control: NEAT for AOD transport in neutral-atom arrays, an FPGA-based quantum data processing unit measuring NVQLink round-trip latency, Lean-verified QCCD co-design (QCCDCert) scaling to 512 qubits, MLIR-based circuit cutting (QWeaver), and fidelity-predictive multi-vendor QPU scheduling.

ranked.headline: Quantum key distribution and entanglement move onto deployed metropolitan and intercity links
ranked.summary: New preprints report a four-city entanglement QKD network, CV entanglement over deployed fibre and comb-based shared infrastructure, alongside finite-key proofs.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the transition of quantum communication from laboratory testbeds to field-deployed links with rigorous finite-size security accounting. A four-city Slovak entanglement-based QKD network delivers keys in real time and is benchmarked against finite-key bounds. Continuous-variable entanglement is distributed over deployed metropolitan fibre (23 km and 450 m) using independent coherent receivers and digital processing. An optical-frequency-comb infrastructure unifies precision timing and 100 Mbit/s classical data on a shared 100 km fibre. On the theory side, variable-length MDI QKD gains a finite-size proof that accounts for source imperfections, with key rates over horizontal links beyond 80 km. Finite-key MIMO CV-QKD is analysed for satellite channels. Related work extends protocols and media: frequency-bin quantum secret sharing with 20 MHz basis switching, and pre-amplified two-mode squeezed microwave states over open air. Adjacent photonics results address postselection-free CHSH violation and fusion-based computing under partial photon distinguishability.

ranked.headline: DESI-era tests probe whether dark energy evolves, crosses the phantom divide, or is Λ
ranked.summary: New reconstructions, model comparisons, independent SN Ia pipelines and CMB forecasts test the DESI-driven w0–wa departure from ΛCDM from several directions.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is whether DESI BAO or full-shape data, combined with CMB, supernova and lensing probes, require dark energy that departs from a cosmological constant. At the model level, three one-parameter vacuum histories are compared within VCDM: F42 is favored by AIC when supernovae are included, while the Bayesian evidence is assessed separately. A DESI DR1 full-shape analysis finds that the scalar-field Fading Dark Sector model outperforms CPL w0–wa. Two non-parametric reconstructions of the effective dark-energy density and gravitational response, using CMB, BAO, SNe and LSS or DES lensing data, report a phantom-divide crossing near z≈0.5–0.7, and one also asks whether dark energy clusters. On systematics, LEMAITRE and a ZTF/SNLS/HSC calibration effort provide SN Ia datasets independent of existing compilations to test the w–w_a tension. A Bayesian forecast examines whether Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 can distinguish w0waCDM from ΛCDM shadow models. Separate preprints address 21 cm signatures of boosted dark matter and the influence of astrophysical priors on new-physics evidence in pulsar timing arrays.

ranked.headline: Emulators, differentiable codes and field-level models target survey-era cosmological inference
ranked.summary: LSST Year 1 and DESI DR2 analyses are paired with fast emulators, differentiable spectra codes and field-level Lyman-alpha models, plus new FRB and GW probes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is fast, accurate theory and forward modeling for upcoming survey analyses. A Hi-COLA-trained emulator gives the nonlinear matter power spectrum in Cubic Galileon gravity for LSST Year 1. bihalofit-JAX supplies a differentiable nonlinear bispectrum and projected statistics, reported orders of magnitude faster. For the Lyman-alpha forest, a cubic-order EFT forward model (validated on CAMELS and Sherwood) yields BAO shift predictions and priors, while a 3D U-Net reproduces P1D, bispectrum and trispectrum across TNG and FLAMINGO. A secondary thread applies alternative probes: a physics-informed neural network tests GR with DESI DR2, fast radio bursts constrain baryon distribution and Ωm–w from 125 localized events, and Padé cosmography is forecast for gravitational-wave sirens. The QCD equation-of-state study is peripheral.

ranked.headline: Quantum learning shifts to fixed feature maps, calibration and ensembles to ease training
ranked.summary: Eight preprints address noise, concentration and training costs in quantum learning via fixed circuits, calibration, ensembles and physics-informed kernels.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is reducing the burden of training variational quantum models. Several works avoid or limit parametrized-circuit optimization: a fixed multi-layer quantum extreme learning machine with a linear readout fitted via MMD for generative modeling, and Soft-MoQE, which gates fixed quantum feature maps classically and matches trainable QNNs on MNIST. Others target trainability directly through reusable calibration against hardware noise, Bagging and AdaBoost for variational regressors, and contractive layers with one trainable parameter on Rydberg arrays. An empirical study examines how entanglement, locality and bandwidth scaling control exponential concentration in quantum kernels and extreme learning. Physics-oriented applications include an inverse participation ratio kernel for quantum phases and JEPA-based world models inferring Hamiltonian parameters from few-body dynamics. All items are preprints.

ranked.headline: Spin and charge symmetry enforced in quantum state loading, diagonalization, and chemistry simulation
ranked.summary: Spin-adapted sampling and MPS loading yield exact symmetry sectors while sparse and first-quantised methods cut sample and Toffoli costs.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is encoding physical structure to reduce quantum simulation cost, with symmetry as the clearest case. Spin-adapted SqDRIFT completes sampled configurations to enforce S^2 and return exact spin eigenstates. A circuit loads U(1)×SU(2)-symmetric matrix product states from spin-adapted reduced tensors, cutting Toffoli counts for fault-tolerant algorithms. Other items exploit structure differently: sparse quantum prolate diagonalization uses compressed sensing to reduce sample complexity from O(N_s) to O(log N_s) with a trapped-ion demonstration, a sum-of-squares representation lowers first-quantised phase estimation Toffoli cost by up to 16x, and a canonical polyadic decomposition of Coulomb-like potentials reduces T-gate scaling. On the classical side, F2-linear partitioning enables Pauli propagation beyond 10^11 strings. Quantum-walk search on complete bipartite graphs is also realized on hardware.

ranked.headline: Formal verification and exact certification tighten quantum compilers and error-correcting codes
ranked.summary: Eight preprints pair compilation and fault-tolerance resource savings with Lean-checked or exact certification of circuits and codes.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is fault-tolerant quantum software where resource reduction is paired with correctness guarantees. Compilation work includes MARBLE, which synthesizes OpenQASM block encodings from matrix formulas, qlin, which rewrites dynamic-circuit branches and decoders with a Lean 4-verified translation validator, and PRISM, which keeps multiple logical-gate realizations open during dual-rail routing. Verification work includes a formally verified Shor order-finding harness with O(n^(2+ε)) gate cost, QECLean for machine-verified code specification, and QEDist for exact distance certification of stabilizer codes, including fault distance. Architecture-level papers formalize reaction depth, showing constant-depth coherent Boolean arithmetic, and use Block Checks with Pareto tree search for state-preparation depth-operation trade-offs. Formal verification is not common to every item.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-based optical, spin and magnon responses proposed to probe unconventional magnetic order
ranked.summary: Eight preprints propose transport, optical and magnonic signatures that identify and exploit altermagnetic, odd-parity, noncoplanar and spin-nematic order.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is theory that ties measurable responses to the symmetry of unconventional magnetic order. For altermagnets, noncoplanar antiferromagnets and odd-parity magnets, the proposed probes are octupolar magneto-optical effects, nonlinear spin generation and spin photocurrent, and charge-spin selection rules with temporal-spectral separation in transport. Twist engineering of collinear bilayers is proposed to give quasicrystalline altermagnets with high-order spin polarization. On the magnon side, single magnons and bound magnon pairs in pyrochlore spin-nematics give competing thermal Hall contributions that allow field-tunable sign reversal. In CrI3 nanotubes, an axial field produces a conical phase and a large pseudo-orbital magnon moment. In BiFeO3, gate-controlled domain boundaries modulate nonreciprocal magnons in a proposed transistor. Cavity photon condensation driven by scalar spin chirality is a more peripheral item. All eight are preprints.

ranked.headline: Inference pipelines for gravitational-wave, lensing, cluster and reionization data are built and tested
ranked.summary: Seven preprints dated 12-19 November 2026 present samplers, ML components and pipeline comparisons for LISA, Euclid, LSST DESC and SKA analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is building and validating inference infrastructure for forthcoming cosmological datasets, though the items do not all concern sampler efficiency. ASPIRE reuses existing posteriors for joint cosmological and population inference with dark sirens, reporting 6-28x speedups over reanalysis. samsara++ implements trans-dimensional MCMC in C++/CUDA for LISA global fits with overlapping Galactic binaries and noise. The LSST DESC cluster pipeline is validated on cosmoDC2 mocks, constraining Omega_c and sigma_8. Euclid work addresses ML components: strong-lens detection depends strongly on training-set composition, image format and ensembling, while EuclidFM learns 128-dim embeddings from Q1 photometry. SciPIC-lite provides a public Python library for flexible HOD modelling of clustering observables. SKA SDC3b compares 16 teams' EoR pipelines and finds inter-team variability, which bears on cross-validation of inference methods.

ranked.headline: Compilers target pulse latency and coupling-constrained routing; simulators scale noisy and QEC circuit analysis
ranked.summary: New preprints tie compilation to hardware cost: pulse latency in SCOPE and two-qubit counts in quspect, alongside faster noisy and QEC circuit simulation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is compilation judged by hardware-level cost rather than abstract gate count. SCOPE uses an operator Schmidt time surrogate to reduce pulse execution latency and is reported to outperform EPOC on 104 benchmarks. The quspect SDK selects routings after coupling-constrained resynthesis, reaching 0.616x the two-qubit gates of Qiskit O3 on 55 circuits across five targets. A second, adjacent thread concerns classical simulation of noisy and error-corrected circuits: MASQ, pre-trajectory sampling with mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels, and Clifford-augmented matrix product states for coherent noise. The QAOA coverage study uses exact references and hardware diagnostics, and the fluid-flow paper pairs reduced models with surface-code estimates; both are application-side rather than compilation results.

ranked.headline: Pulse-level control proposals target multi-qubit and mediator-assisted gates on atomic and solid-state qubits
ranked.summary: Seven November preprints advance control for entangling gates, mediator qubits and state preparation, including a Rydberg phase-estimation demonstration on 19 atoms.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control design for multi-qubit and mediator-mediated operations. One preprint proposes an analytically specified CCZ gate for neutral atoms under finite Rydberg interactions, compared with a fast antiblockade scheme. Another proposes reset-assisted control, analyzed with quantum trajectories, in which noisy mediator qubits drive high-fidelity gates on long-lived data qubits. The geodesiq package combines adiabatic and diabatic control for state transfer. Krotov optimization with a single local field prepares GHZ-type states in an XXZ chain, with fidelities above 0.927. An analog Rydberg simulator performs phase estimation on up to 19 atoms via Loschmidt echoes. Peripheral items cover bosonic Fock-state stabilization through Fock-space currents and a proposed Fe2+:forsterite qubit simulated at 99.9% fidelity. All results here are preprints, and most are proposals or simulations.

ranked.headline: Disorder and defects shape Hall plateaus and generate or tune orbital transport responses
ranked.summary: Six November 2026 preprints treat disorder, defects and scattering as determinants of Chern plateaus, orbital Hall and magnetoelectric responses, and magnetotransport.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is that disorder and defects are treated as determinants of transport rather than perturbations, though the items differ in scope. In twisted bilayer MoTe2, layer-dependent disorder shapes integer and fractional Chern plateau widths and transitions. Orbital-response studies extend this: Kubo-Bastin Chebyshev calculations address disorder robustness and tunability of the quadrupole-origin orbital Hall effect in a centrosymmetric sp3 lattice; point defects enhance and activate orbital magnetoelectric responses in an orbital antiferromagnet; and structural and electrostatic disorder, including amorphous graphene, yields orbital Hall currents absent in pristine systems. The multi-Weyl work instead goes beyond constant relaxation time, including orbital moment and intervalley scattering. The orbital exchange study in MoS2 concerns clean-limit Hall responses without spin or spin-orbit coupling.

ranked.headline: Ultrafast optical and electrical pulses deterministically write skyrmions and compensated magnetic states
ranked.summary: New preprints show picosecond laser and spin-orbit-torque writing of skyrmions, antiferromagnetic textures and compensated states, plus probes of AFM switching.
ranked.synthesis: The main thread is deterministic writing of magnetic order with ultrafast optical or electrical stimuli. Picosecond circularly polarized pulses write fixed-chirality Néel skyrmions in Co/Pt, with chirality set by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Laser pulses imprint antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer within picoseconds. Atomistic simulations find all-optical helicity-independent switching in GdCo with as little as 1.5 at.% Gd. In triangular artificial spin ice, spin-orbit torque switching and planar Hall readout write and read a compensated state electrically. Two probe-oriented studies connect more loosely: pulsed-field MOKE up to 60 T on the metamagnetic transition in Fe2Mo3O8, and NV magnetometry of zero-field bistability and thermally activated switching in antiferromagnetic CrPS4 trilayers.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 documentation defines survey coverage, masks, photometry validation and photo-z-based galaxy properties
ranked.summary: Five Euclid DR1 papers appeared on 2026-11-12, documenting the release contents, survey status, masks, photometry validation and PHZ galaxy-property processing.
ranked.synthesis: The items form a coordinated documentation set for Euclid Data Release 1, not a set of cosmological analyses. The overview describes a two-part release of images, spectra and catalogues covering about a billion objects from wide and deep fields, while the survey paper reports 2100 deg² of Wide Survey area. Supporting papers describe photometric masks, which trace spatial variations in survey properties, and the PHZ pipeline, which uses NNPZ nearest-neighbour inference with a COSMOS reference sample to derive non-cosmological galaxy properties. The main quantified check compares multi-band photometry with the JWST-based COSMOS2025 catalogue: median offsets are mostly within 10%, largest in NIR deep model-fitting. None of the items presents cosmological results.

ranked.headline: Quantum sensors and detectors probe dark matter and new physics across lab, space, and astrophysical settings
ranked.summary: Reviews and a new detector proposal converge on quantum-enabled searches for dark matter, BSM physics, and gravitational waves.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of quantum-enabled or precision detection to test physics beyond the Standard Model. One review covers direct dark matter detection, including detector technologies, results since 2020, and future experiments. Proceedings discuss atomic clocks, atom interferometers, and magnetometers in space for BSM and dark matter searches. A white paper frames multi-messenger AGN observations and AGN-surrounding dark matter as BSM laboratories. A colloquium links isotope enrichment and detection to proposed quantum tests with radioactive atomic clocks. The one new detector concept proposes gravitational-wave sensing via massive-particle interferometry, where a gravitationally induced phase along a closed loop encodes the signal. The items are mixed in scope, but together they emphasize complementary laboratory, space-based, and astrophysical routes.

ranked.headline: Higher-order statistical modelling recovers density and lens-mass fields from survey observables
ranked.summary: Five preprints extend redshift-space, field-level, lensing and systematics-deprojection methods to extract more field information from galaxy and lensing data.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is reconstructing underlying fields from observables through explicit statistical modelling of higher-order or field-level information. In redshift space, a tracer-centred density-split model derives bias and an empirical cosmological description, while the isotropic galaxy 4PCF is shown to have vanishing parity-odd redshift-space distortion contributions after line-of-sight averaging. A faster field-level likelihood for large-scale galaxy surveys forecasts sigma(fNL)=4.1. In weak lensing, roulette amplitudes beyond flexion improve least-squares lens-mass reconstruction for clusters. For SPHEREx, an information-criterion-driven, non-linear deprojection addresses angular imaging systematics, tested on lognormal mocks. What is new is the focus on analytic, likelihood-based and systematics-aware treatment of the field, rather than compression alone.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-based frameworks extend classification of topological and quantum many-body phases
ranked.summary: Five preprints in mid-November 2026 extend symmetry-based classification, from the SymTFT and subsystem SPT response theory to higher-order and half-chiral phases.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is how symmetry structure constrains and classifies gapped and topological phases. A review presents the SymTFT framework for generalized symmetries, anomalies, and phase classification. A lattice response theory for subsystem SPT phases links response actions to cluster entanglers. Three further works concern lattice topology under unconventional symmetry: an intrinsic chiral higher-order topological phase stabilized by a single diagonal reflection in a quarter-plane, phases protected by half-chiral symmetry acting on one sublattice with real-space invariants, and a generalized spectral localizer giving Z and Z2 invariants for hinge, Dirac-node, and valley modes. What is new is the extension of protecting symmetries and of invariants, rather than a single shared method.

ranked.headline: Euclid DR1 calibration chains for NIR imaging, spectroscopy and ground-based colours are documented
ranked.summary: Five Euclid DR1 preprints document the calibration and processing chains, with performance assessed against mission requirements.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the instrument-level processing and calibration underlying Euclid DR1. The papers cover NISP near-infrared processing and data products, NIR astrometric calibration with distortion modelling, quality control and residuals against Gaia DR3 reaching 30 mas, and SIR spectroscopic calibration, which models the focal plane globally to meet wavelength and flux requirements. Ground-based optical imaging over about 2500 deg2 supplies colours, with photometric stability and depth validated for photo-z and PSF calibration. A calibration strategy paper reviews plan design, implementation and performance against requirements, including corrections for flux, astrometry, PSF, shear and wavelength. What is new is the documented performance of these chains at DR1 scale. The items describe pipelines and validation, not cosmological constraints.

ranked.headline: Resonant nanostructures tune chiral, magnetic and THz response via coupling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints quantify resonance tuning via strong coupling, anion exchange and hybridization across silicon, perovskite and plasmonic platforms.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is control of resonant optical response through coupling, composition or environment. In silicon bound-state-in-continuum metasurfaces, strong coupling between a QBIC and a GMR yields intrinsic circular dichroism of 0.995 at 1653.9 nm with a Q-factor of 1083. In perovskite metasurfaces, MAPbBr3 bound-state-in-continuum resonances shift reversibly and continuously under HCl/HBr vapor anion exchange, establishing chemical reconfiguration as a tuning route. Coupled TiO2 and perovskite-coated microresonators display tunable whispering gallery mode hybridization with non-monotonic behavior. Plasmonic work extends the theme to terahertz instrumentation, where polarization-resilient nanoantenna arrays with fiber coupling report 2.1 mW output and 145 dB dynamic range, and to magnetization via the inverse Faraday effect in a coaxial nanoantenna across five materials. The new element is quantified resonance tuning across chiral, chemical and THz platforms. Most results are numerical or theoretical unless experimental metrics are stated.

ranked.headline: Recovering optical field information from constrained or imperfect measurements
ranked.summary: Recent preprints address specific error sources and resource bottlenecks in structured light, single-pixel, ptychographic and hyperspectral imaging.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the recovery of optical field information from constrained or imperfect measurements, achieved through computation or engineered illumination and readout. Active convolved illumination (arXiv:2611.17471) is reviewed as a framework for preserving optical mode structure through turbulent media via segmented reciprocal-space control. Within single-pixel imaging, a Fourier-domain response-matrix correction (arXiv:2611.19283) addresses quantization errors in binary-encoded Fourier acquisition, whereas arXiv:2611.25700 converts temporal mixing into a measurement resource through a unified calibration and composite-readout framework. A stochastic gradient descent framework for X-ray ptychographic reconstruction (arXiv:2611.24232) reports peak GPU memory reduced to 65% and time to 22% relative to the comparison method. Event-camera Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy (arXiv:2611.26097) reaches real-time widefield spectral acquisition. The modalities differ; the novelty lies in targeted treatment of specific error sources or resource bottlenecks within each.

ranked.headline: Switchable ferroelectric and magnetic order controls excitons and valley states
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show electrical, magnetic and optical handles on exciton and valley states across van der Waals bilayers and heterostructures.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is using an ordered degree of freedom as an external handle on excitonic and valley states in van der Waals materials. In rhombohedrally stacked bilayer WSe2, sliding ferroelectricity gives electrically switchable, hysteretic exciton photoluminescence and Raman response, and in few-layer R-stacked WSe2 it switches dipolar exciton transport and drives dipole reconfiguration toward quadrupolar excitons. In WS2/CrSBr heterostructures, type-II band alignment and magnetic-proximity Zeeman splitting couple valley and magnetic excitons. In WSe2/CrPS4, a light-controlled Néel vector switches valley polarization optically via spin-polarized charge transfer. The NbOCl2 preprint reports room-temperature antiferroelectric switching probed by SHG but does not address valley or exciton states directly. What is new is the breadth of switchable order, magnetic, ferroelectric and optical, applied to valley and exciton control.

ranked.headline: Programmable unitary interferometers for coherent photonic computation and measurement
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend programmable unitary photonic circuits to on-chip interconnects, optical neural networks, modular processors, and spectral measurement.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the use of programmable unitary interferometric circuits as the computational or functional primitive in coherent photonic systems. The preprint 2611.20390 proposes a logarithmic-depth butterfly interferometer architecture for parameter-efficient unitary transformations in coherent optical neural networks, while 2611.21582 builds a modular processor from unitary tiles of fixed mixers and programmable phases, evaluated by numerical fitting. The silicon chip in 2611.23667 uses unequal path lengths between two 8x8 unitary circuits to perform simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering at 0.05 nm resolution. The coherent-lite interconnect in 2611.19254, which combines wavelength and mode multiplexing with self-homodyne detection, is a related on-chip coherent link reaching 103.96 Tb/s aggregate line rate. What is new is the joint emphasis on depth-efficient parameterization, modular tiling of unitary elements, and multifunctional use across computation, measurement, and interconnection.

ranked.headline: Non-Hermitian gain, loss and skin effects reshape edge and scattering behavior
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report edge amplification, self-dual spectral singularities and symmetry-breaking constraints in non-Hermitian gain-loss systems.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints share a common setting: open non-Hermitian systems with gain, loss, or asymmetric coupling, where scattering and spectral properties depart from Hermitian expectations. One item reports an experimental microwave study of universal statistics of reflectivity, transmissivity and absorptivity in multi-port non-Hermitian scattering systems. Another shows that coupled skin-effect channels amplify states bouncing off edges, departing from the usual OBC-within-PBC spectral picture. A third is a theoretical and numerical study of a self-dual spectral singularity in coupled gain and loss ring resonators coupled to a waveguide. The fourth shows that gain-loss induced T-symmetry breaking is forbidden in time-dependent systems, even for random gain-loss distributions. What is new is the combination of statistical universality, edge amplification, and constraints on symmetry breaking, rather than a single unified result. Edge-state physics is represented by only one of the four items.

ranked.headline: Magnon nonlinear processes generate entangled and phase-controlled microwaves
ranked.summary: Recent preprints propose and demonstrate magnon-based routes to phase-controlled and entanglement-oriented microwave sources.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is magnon-mediated nonlinear conversion of spin waves into microwave signals. arXiv:2611.25207 proposes tunable entangled propagating microwaves via three-magnon parametric down-conversion in thin ferromagnetic films. arXiv:2611.26932 demonstrates parametric excitation of nano-scale spin waves with two controlled phase states using a VCMA open-resonator transducer, with lowered threshold. arXiv:2611.21869 extends the magnon picture to optomechanics, reporting an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of -43 MHz in suspended CrSBr membranes. arXiv:2611.16721, on chiral high harmonic generation in NbP, is a distinct nonlinear optical topic. The novelty lies in phase-controlled and entanglement-oriented magnon sources with electrical control.

ranked.headline: Parametric oscillation and electro-optic comb generation in engineered resonators
ranked.summary: Recent preprints demonstrate nonlinear and electro-optic light generation in new platforms, from cryogenic silicon to gain-assisted fiber resonators.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of resonant cavities to shape coherent light through nonlinear or modulated interactions. One work demonstrates telecom-band optical parametric oscillation in a passive silicon microring at 4.5 K under a single continuous-wave pump, with a reported 2.25 mW onset. Another uses a pair of gain-assisted electro-optic fiber ring resonators with intracavity modulation to produce a 1.8 THz flat-top comb for dual-comb spectroscopy. A third shows that intensity-modulated driving near mechanical resonance enlarges optomechanical oscillation amplitude toward the cavity-bandwidth limit and extends frequency comb bandwidth. The fourth, a 60-cm in-vacuum Zerodur cavity, addresses cavity stability for optical lattice atom interferometry rather than light generation. What is new is the demonstration of these processes in specific platforms: cryogenic passive silicon, gain-assisted electro-optic fiber cavities, and modulated optomechanical systems.

ranked.headline: Non-sinusoidal current-phase relations in Josephson junctions for qubit platforms
ranked.summary: Preprints now treat non-sinusoidal Josephson current-phase relations as a design variable for superconducting qubits and qudits.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is treating the Josephson current-phase relation as an engineering variable rather than the ideal sinusoid. The qutrit proposal exploits the second harmonic of the current-phase relation in three-junction loops, with altermagnetic elements mentioned in its abstract. The Al/AlOx/Al study examines non-ergodic area scaling of Andreev transport explicitly against the sinusoidal ideal. Gatemon work reports in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire junctions with gate tunability over GHz and T1 of about 0.2-1 us. The Ge study reports gate-tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits that is independent of junction width, unlike InAs. What is new is the spread of materials platforms and the deliberate departure from conventional junction behavior; all four items are preprints with differing scope and maturity.

ranked.headline: Coupling sign and non-Hermiticity tune flatband and BIC states in photonic structures
ranked.summary: Recent preprints connect coupling sign and non-Hermiticity to flatband and BIC control, and an experiment reports exact mobility edges in a photonic quasicrystal.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the engineering of localized and confined optical modes in photonic platforms, with flat bands and bound states in the continuum as the central theme. Two model-based preprints show that non-Hermiticity and coupling sign govern this behavior: in C2-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs, coupling sign controls BIC merging and flatband formation with reported Q scaling as k^-6, and in one-dimensional non-Hermitian pseudospin lattices, non-Hermiticity embeds compact localized states within a continuum. An experimental preprint realizes exact mobility edges and flat-band states in a two-dimensional photonic quasicrystal using auxiliary subsystems and photonic waveguides. The fourth item, a proposal for antihelical gapless edge states in a photonic metacrystal with staggered bianisotropy, addresses edge states rather than flat bands. What is new is explicit tuning of flatband and BIC physics through coupling sign and non-Hermiticity, together with experimental verification of exact mobility edges.

ranked.headline: Multilayer and metasurface designs tune wavelength-selective thermal radiation
ranked.summary: Inverse-designed multilayers, spacer-tuned metasurfaces and an AM0 optical property database all target wavelength-resolved control of thermal radiation.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is wavelength-resolved control of thermal radiation, where absorption, emission and reflection govern energy conversion. A 16-layer MgO/Si multilayer on tungsten is inverse-designed as a selective emitter for GaSb thermophotovoltaic cells, with a modeled conversion efficiency of 47.0%. A gold-carbon metasurface uses a dielectric spacer to tune gap-mode overlap with carbon, sharpening the infrared roll-off in solar-thermal absorbers. The SpaderOptics database provides reflectivity, absorptivity and emissivity for 21 materials under the AM0 solar spectrum. The photonic Maxwell's demon proposal, which uses one-way dielectric mirrors and wavelength-converting materials in a 3D box to accumulate blackbody radiation, is less directly tied to this thread. The new elements are inverse design of a multilayer emitter, spacer-based gap-mode tuning, and property data under AM0 illumination. All four items are numerical or proposal-stage.

ranked.headline: Accidental BICs in photonic lattices and metasurfaces depend on parity and nonlocality
ranked.summary: Recent preprints recast accidental BIC existence in terms of radiation-source parity and spatially nonlocal scattering response.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the characterization of bound states in the continuum (BICs), modes that remain confined despite lying within the radiation continuum of open photonic systems. Two preprints address accidental BICs directly: one shows that in vertically asymmetric photonic lattices they are governed by radiation-source parity and can be recovered through parity restoration, while the other models metasurface BICs as converging reflection and transmission zeros and concludes that accidental BICs require spatially nonlocal response. A third preprint studies Berry phase and topological quasi-bound states in Möbius resonators, reporting a phase that depends on the mode. The fourth item, a microwave study of higher-order topological hinge states in an all-dielectric woodpile photonic crystal, shares the topological photonic context but is less directly tied to the BIC framing. The new element is the expression of accidental BIC existence in terms of parity and nonlocality.

ranked.headline: Energy spectra of bilayer graphene from q-deformed models and momentum-space QMC
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend bilayer graphene spectral calculations to q-deformed magnetic-field models and remote-band quantum Monte Carlo.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is the computation of energy spectra in low-dimensional and few-body quantum systems. Two preprints address bilayer graphene directly. The first derives spectra, currents, and thermodynamics for q-deformed Dirac oscillator models of monolayer and bilayer graphene in a magnetic field. The second applies momentum-space quantum Monte Carlo to twisted bilayer graphene, including remote bands and testing the validity of flat-band projection. What is new is the deformed-algebra treatment of the magnetic-field problem and the explicit assessment of interaction effects beyond projected flat-band models in the twisted case. A third preprint computes trion energy levels in bulk semiconductors across hole-to-electron mass ratios using finite-element and Gaussian expansion methods; it shares the spectral-calculation approach but not the graphene context.
